We now run on 1,200 repositories. When we launched Patchwork CI, we promised it would always be free for open source, and plenty of people told us we were crazy. "How will you make money?" they asked.

Today, about 900 of those 1,200 repositories are open source.

What really surprised me was the data. Across all those repos, 1 in 7 CI failures turned out to be a flaky test. That is countless hours of developer time wasted on red builds that were not real failures.

Open source did more than give us users. It gave us data, feedback, and a community. Our most-requested feature, GitLab support, came straight from OSS maintainers, and we shipped it on November 12.

Giving back is not charity. It is strategy.

#OpenSource #DevOps #CI #DeveloperExperience #BuildInPublic

We built an app we were proud of, and almost nobody used it.

Hardware is hard, so here is our story.

Our first production run at Shelfwise did not go as planned. 400 labels shipped with a faulty battery contact.

As a young hardware startup, it would have been easy to cut corners. That is not who we are. We decided to recall and replace every one of those 400 labels at our own cost, which set us back about $7,000. Painful? Absolutely. Worth it? 100%, because trust is everything.

We did not stop there. We introduced a 100% contact test at the factory, and since then we have seen zero contact failures across 6,000 labels.

Mistakes do not define you. How you respond to them does. To all the hardware founders out there: own your mistakes, fix them fast, and build systems so they never happen again.
